what_its_for: Sevelamer carbonate is used to control high phosphorus (phosphate) levels in your blood. This is a common problem in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who are on dialysis. Too much phosphorus in your blood can weaken your bones, damage your heart and blood vessels, and cause serious health problems. This medicine works by binding to phosphorus from the food you eat in your stomach and intestines so your body absorbs less of it.
how_to_take: Take sevelamer carbonate WITH meals — this is very important. It only works if you take it while eating because it needs to bind to the phosphorus in your food. Swallow the tablets whole with water. Do NOT crush, chew, or break the tablets. If you are using the powder (oral suspension), mix the entire packet with the amount of water listed on your prescription label, stir well, and drink the mixture right away. Do not save mixed powder for later.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your phosphorus blood levels. Common starting doses are 800 mg to 1600 mg taken three times a day with each meal. Your dose may be adjusted over time. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose with your next meal as usual. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Since this medicine only works when taken with food, there is no benefit in taking it between meals.
storage: Store sevelamer carbonate tablets and unopened powder packets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you have mixed powder that you did not use, throw it away — do not save it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking sevelamer carbonate at the same time as other medicines unless your doctor says it is okay. It can interfere with how some other medicines are absorbed. Take other medicines either 1 hour before or 3 hours after sevelamer carbonate. Also, try to follow a low-phosphorus diet as recommended by your kidney dietitian — this medicine works best when combined with diet changes. Avoid high-phosphorus foods such as dairy products, nuts, cola drinks, processed meats, and fast food unless your dietitian tells you otherwise.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: severe constipation, stomach pain, bloating, or vomiting that does not go away; difficulty swallowing or swallowing tablets feels stuck; black or bloody stools; signs of a blockage in your intestines (no bowel movements, severe cramping); or if your blood phosphorus levels are still high after starting treatment. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, or if you are starting any new medicines including over-the-counter drugs or supplements.
when_it_works: Sevelamer carbonate starts working right away during meals to bind phosphorus from your food. However, you may not feel different because high phosphorus often has no noticeable symptoms. Your doctor will check your blood phosphorus levels regularly (usually every 1 to 3 months) to see if the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it every day with meals even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution as constipation and bowel problems may be more likely. Children: Sevelamer carbonate can be used in children aged 6 years and older who are on dialysis; the dose will be based on your child's body size. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Sevelamer carbonate may reduce the absorption of important vitamins and nutrients, so your doctor may recommend vitamin supplements. People with bowel problems: Tell your doctor if you have a history of swallowing disorders, severe stomach or bowel problems, or have recently had bowel surgery, as this medicine may not be safe for you.
